articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 4
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's rankings are here to help.
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Steelers-Browns game.

Week 4 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 @ CAR

Six touchdowns in three games is quite the feat. It's LaDainian Tomlinson stuff (2006).
 2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR1 vs LAC

The league leader in fantasy points seems unstoppable, regardless of matchup.
 3. Josh Allen, QB1 vs NE

He has rushed for two touchdowns in each game. Can the Patriots stop him?
 4. Bijan Robinson, RB2 @ NO

He has scored more than 30 points in two of three games. 
 5. Lamar Jackson, QB2 vs TEN

The 50 rushing yards from the Week 3 win are a terrific sign.
 6. Ja'Marr Chase, WR2 vs JAX

 7. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR3 @ CAR

 8. Puka Nacua, WR4 @ PHI

 
 9. Jonathan Taylor, RB3 @ WSH

More than 20 touches each week, which is nice when he doesn't score a TD or two.
 10. Derrick Henry, RB4 vs TEN

You know he always wants to shine against his former Titans teammates. 
 11. Kenneth Walker III, RB5 @ LV

The volume was down a bit, but he scores TDs. Note: Chiefs are on a bye in Week 5. Plan ahead!
 12. Christian McCaffrey, RB6 vs DEN

The 49ers are keeping his volume well in check. It's a tough matchup with the Broncos this week.
 13. Brock Purdy, QB3 vs DEN

 14. Patrick Mahomes, QB4 @ LV

 15. Tyler Shough, QB5 vs ATL

 16. Trevor Lawrence, QB6 @ CIN

His investors could have used the rushing TD he gave to a teammate on Sunday.
 17. Chris Olave, WR5 vs ATL

 18. Ashton Jeanty, RB7 vs KC

 19. James Cook III, RB8 vs NE

The argument that his QB steals the rushing TDs doesn't work. Cook is great.
 20. Jalen Hurts, QB7 vs LAR

Mild concern over a disappointing Monday effort. The Rams visit Philly Sunday. That's not great, either.
 21. Joe Burrow, QB8 vs JAX

 22. Bryce Young, QB9 vs DET

 23. Matthew Stafford, QB10 @ PHI

If a third-string QB can light up the Eagles, what do you think Stafford can do?
 24. CeeDee Lamb, WR6 @ HOU

Some may try to fade top Cowboys against the Texans, but that is a mistake. 
 25. Drake London, WR7 @ NO

Any worries about his production ended in Week 3. London dominated the Packers. 
 26. Marcus Mariota, QB11 vs IND

One of the best backups in the business remains a solid investment this week.
 27. Kyler Murray, QB12 vs MIA

The matchup with Miami -- not his play -- drives this aggressive projection.

articles.headline: Texans get WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back vs. Cowboys
articles.description: The winless Texans got good news Friday as star wide receiver Nico Collins is set to return Sunday from a hamstring injury that forced him to miss Houston's last two games.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- After a two-game absence, Houston Texans wideout Nico Collins is set to return against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4.

Collins practiced Wednesday and Thursday this week after hurting his hamstring during a Week 2 practice.

The injury forced Collins to miss Weeks 2 and 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals and Indianapolis Colts as the Texans went 0-2. Without Collins, the offense averaged 11.5 points per game, but Houston scored 31 against the Buffalo Bills with the Pro Bowl wideout in the lineup in the season opener.

Coach DeMeco Ryans knows how vital the Texans' star receiver is to their offense and hopes he provides a major boost.

"Everyone understands and knows the type of player Nico is," Ryans said Wednesday. "He's an explosive playmaker any time he's touching the ball; any time he's on the field, he's a threat. Defenses have to prepare for him and they have to do different things to adjust for him, so we're happy to have Nico back."

Houston sits 0-3, and this week is a borderline must-win game for the Texans to keep any hopes of making the playoffs alive. The only time a team ever started 0-4 and made the postseason was in 1992, when the Chargers did it.

The winless start is disappointing considering Houston had Super Bowl aspirations. But 0-3 is where the Texans sat after three weeks in 2025 before finishing the regular season by winning 12 of their remaining 14 games.

Houston's offense also gets back starting right guard Ed Ingram, who missed the last two games.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Jadon Sancho willing to wait for January move
articles.description: Jadon Sancho is happy to wait to sign for a club. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Free agent Jadon Sancho is happy to wait to sign for a club, while Tomás Araújo is subject to interest from Manchester United and Chelsea.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Jadon Sancho is willing to hold out until January as a free agent before making a decision, if the right offer doesn't arrive before then, reports TEAMtalk. The former Manchester United and Borussia Dortmund winger is a free agent, following his exit from Old Trafford at the end of his contract in the summer. The 26-year-old has been linked with a whole host of clubs since, but is yet to make a decision on his future, with nothing advanced on his next club.

- Manchester United and Chelsea are monitoring a deal for Benfica defender Tomás Araújo, according to TEAMTalk. The 24-year-old is claimed to be on the radar of several Premier League clubs, but it's United and Chelsea who are most keen. Araujo, who can play center back and right-back, recently signed a contract extension until 2031, making an exit in January unlikely. However, with a release clause valued at £68 million, clubs could pursue a switch anyway

- Juventus are preparing a huge rebuild over the next year, with Tuttosport naming a whole host of potential transfer targets for the Italian club. In the goalkeeping ranks, Alisson Becker is claimed to be a player of interest, as he could leave Liverpool at the end of the season as a free agent. In defence, Oumar Solet of Udinese is viewed as an option, while RB Leipzig ace David Raum and Crystal Palace star Tyrick Mitchell are also on the Bianconeri's radar. Napoli stalwart Stanislav Lobotka, Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic, and Real Madrid playmaker Brahim Díaz are touted as options for the central ranks. Meanwhile, Crystal Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta could be a striker arrival.

- João Félix is keen on making a return to Barcelona next year, when the Portuguese international's contract with Al Nassr is set to expire. That's according to Sport, which reports that the 27-year-old has his sights set on a return to the Champions League after a recent resurgence in his career in the Saudi Pro League. Felix previously spent a year on loan with Barcelona from Atletico Madrid, where he made 44 appearances with 10 goals and six assists. Now back in form, and eyeing a possible free transfer, a return to the Nou Camp is on his mind, though the report claims that he is not viewed as a priority target.

- Juventus have declared that Kenan Yildiz and Kerim Alajbegovic are "untouchable" in future transfer markets, with the club keen to build around the pair, reports La Gazzetta. articles.headline: Joey Porter Jr. without designation, could debut for Cowboys
articles.description: Newly acquired Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. does not carry an injury designation after practicing the past two days following his trade from the Steelers.
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- Newly acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will be available to make his Dallas Cowboys debut Sunday against the Houston Texans.

Porter, who prior to joining Dallas had been ruled out of Thursday's game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns after saying his back was tight, practiced the past two days with the Cowboys and carries no injury designation into Sunday.

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan after practice Friday, executive vice president Stephen Jones said, "We actually think Joey Porter will get snaps."

Before practice, coach Brian Schottenheimer spoke positively about Porter's chances but did not fully commit to the cornerback playing. Schottenheimer wanted Porter to "stack a second day" after what he called a "really impressive" first practice Thursday.

"I think we've got a really good plan that, if he does play, where we will use him and what that will look like," Schottenheimer said. "But adding the red zone defenses in there today will be a big part of us feeling comfortable about doing it. But like I said [Thursday], he's trending in the right way and he's working really hard at it."

The Cowboys acquired Porter from the Steelers late Wednesday night for a 2027 sixth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick.

With a smile, Porter said Thursday that his back was "feeling better."

"We're just trying to take things day by day, and if everything looks good, then we should be out there," Porter said.

Porter has not played in a game since the Steelers' wild-card loss to the Texans in January. While still learning the Cowboys' defense, he knows what Houston likes to do offensively.

"I think it really just gave me the utmost confidence because I feel like I played well last time I played them in the playoffs," Porter said. "So now the first time I'm suiting up, hopefully suit up, it'll be against them. I mean, that would be ideal. I'm pretty used to their scheme and what they want to do with [C.J. Stroud], and I think I could be a matchup for that."

The Cowboys will be without linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) for the third straight game and cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) for the second straight game.

Cornerback Shavon Revel (knee/ankle) was a full participant Friday after being limited the first two practices of the week and does not carry an injury designation. Safety Malik Hooker, who fractured a forearm in the season opener, is set to return after missing the past two games.

articles.headline: Eagles' DeVonta Smith out vs. Rams with hamstring injury
articles.description: Eagles WR DeVonta Smith will miss Sunday's game due to a lingering hamstring injury and will be joined on the sideline by linebacker Zack Baun (concussion).
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Eagles have ruled out wide receiver DeVonta Smith and linebacker Zack Baun for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.

Smith played 100% of the offensive snaps in Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears but was unable to practice this week due to a hamstring injury.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts will be operating without two of his top pass catchers in Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee). Dontayvion Wicks is expected to assume the role of No. 1 receiver this week, with rookie Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper in line for larger roles as well.

"Being me, the player I am, I already have that confidence," Wicks said of taking on that job.

Baun, who has a concussion, played 92% of the snaps against Chicago before being replaced in the lineup late in the game by Jeremiah Trotter Jr. He has made the Pro Bowl each of the past two seasons while establishing himself as one of the top off-ball linebackers in the game.

Trotter will step in for Baun opposite Jihaad Campbell as the Eagles face the No. 1 offense in the NFL in total yards (418 per game).

"I have to make sure that I'm ready so if I go in there, I've got to make sure I'm doing my part to help the team win," Trotter said. "You don't want to step into a role and be a liability out there, so I'm making sure I'm prepared just like every single week."

Smith missed a good portion of training camp with a hamstring injury, and he was on the injury report last week but was able to suit up against the Bears.

articles.headline: Cucurella: Too soon to judge Mourinho's Madrid amid poor start
articles.description: Marc Cucurella has acknowledged Real Madrid have not started the season as they would have liked under new coach José Mourinho, but he says the team must be judged at the end of the campaign, not now.
articles.body:
Marc Cucurella has acknowledged Real Madrid have not started the season as they would have liked under new coach José Mourinho, but he says the team must be judged at the end of the campaign, not now.

Madrid have suffered two defeats in their opening seven LaLiga games, against Real Betis and Atlético Madrid, leaving them six points behind early leaders Barcelona.

- Torres forced out of Spain squad; Madrid's Espí gets 1st call-up

- De la Fuente says beloved Yamal puts 'magic' at service of Spain

- UEFA receives Madrid dossier on Barça-Negreira case

Cucurella, speaking in a news conference on Friday while on international duty with world champions Spain, said Madrid's new project needs time to take shape.

"It's all a process," Cucurella said. "With the national team, the foundations have been laid over many years -- with the [same] coach, too.

"At Madrid, we have just started with a new manager and it's too soon to speak. Some players only had a week-long preseason before starting.

"The beginning of the season hasn't been what we all hoped for, but it's a process and we will see where we are at the end of the campaign."

Cucurella has picked up where he left off for Spain at the World Cup in the summer, impressing in UEFA Nations League victories over England and Croatia during the last week.

It has led to suggestions the left back -- a €55 million ($62m) summer signing for Madrid from Chelsea -- is better suited to playing for his country than his club.

"It's not even been 10 games yet," Cucurella responded. "There are things to improve [with Madrid], of course. We basically had no preseason, while it's a new club for me.

"I have to adapt to my new teammates and give my best so that the player you see with the national team is the same player with Real Madrid."

Cucurella's form for Chelsea and Spain not only prompted Madrid to sign him in the summer, but also led to him being named among the 30 nominees to win this year's Ballon d'Or.

He is also in the rare position of playing alongside two of the favourites -- Kylian Mbappé with Madrid and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal with Spain -- but would not pick between the two.

"If it was up to me to vote, I would vote for myself," he joked when asked to name his winner.

"But no, two of the candidates to win it are teammates, so who whoever wins it, I will be happy."

Cucurella and Spain are back in action on Saturday when they host Czechia in Oviedo looking to make it three wins from three in the Nations League.

They then close the extended international break with a trip to Croatia on Tuesday.
